why: The refusal rule was measured before it was applied corpus-wide, because a rate is not evidence that a rule is right. A deterministic sample of 24 refused rows -- eight per failure type, ordered by candidate id -- showed the rule was wrong far more often than the evidence was.

stages.false_positives_found: dangling-conjunction stripped terminal punctuation before testing, so a complete attributed quotation ('...\u201d Glenn said.') matched; unmatched-quote fired on any window beginning or ending inside a longer quotation
unmatched-quote still ignored the source boundary that the punctuation rule respected

stages.state: after aligning the quote rule to the source boundary

controls_still_refused: dangling conjunction with no terminal punctuation
conclusion: 279 of 11,018 became 0 of 11,018 once two false-positive rules were corrected -- roughly a 98% false-positive rate in the original check. No stored passage in this corpus is truncated: the 220-character cut was entirely in the results serialisation, not in segmentation. The three rows previously reported as genuinely incomplete were all false positives, including the Joe Burrow caption line.
